confirmed_proposal_compatibility_finding.severity: Must resolve before application; no demonstrated production P0/P1 reachability
confirmed_proposal_compatibility_finding.finding: An owning thread can fail a nested acquire(timeout=0) if another waiter temporarily holds the Condition bookkeeping mutex. Original same-owner RLock succeeds immediately in this case. Timed Condition entry happens before the owner branch, so the reentrant exception does not apply.
confirmed_proposal_compatibility_finding.evidence: release_fair_lock_proposal.py _ReentrantGate.acquire initial Condition.acquire precedes _owner == owner. FileLock promises reentrancy per path/thread; task_store.py includes timeout=0 use.
confirmed_proposal_compatibility_finding.recommendation: Retain same-owner immediate reentrancy independently of competing bookkeeping lock entry, while preserving invalid-timeout validation. Add a deterministic public FileLock nested zero-timeout case with a competing thread held at bookkeeping entry.

earlier_findings_corrected_in_reviewed_b: Queued handoff now rechecks deadline before assigning ownership.
Initial bookkeeping mutex uses timed acquire and finally release.
Underlying RLock timed entry again validates NaN/infinity/>TIMEOUT_MAX rather than allowing NaN busy-spin or silent uncontended infinity.
Free nonzero acquisition rechecks elapsed deadline; zero-timeout free acquisition remains immediate.
sound_parts: FIFO ordering is by enrollment in the explicit deque, not absolute thread start time; an unrelated arriving thread cannot bypass existing tokens.
Queue token exists throughout wait and is removed with notify_all in finally on timeout or wait exception; no empty-deque head access during own waiting lifetime.
Nested depth tracks same-thread recursive entry; only the owner can release the gate.
FileLock class, registry lookup, platform lock/unlock, filesystem handle initialization/fsync and cleanup ASTs are unchanged from actual production.
OS advisory exclusion and cross-process behavior remain unchanged; FIFO fairness applies only within the process.
ownership_limitations: Direct gate release rejects a non-owner before changing gate depth.

Existing FileLock.release mutates instance/state depths and may unlock the file before gate owner validation for a wrong-thread release. This pre-existing unsupported-use behavior is unchanged; the proposal does not make cross-thread release safe.
Thread identity reuse after a thread exits while owning a lock remains an inherited RLock-like boundary.
deadline_limitations: Condition.wait must reacquire its bookkeeping mutex before returning/cleaning up. Python thread scheduling can delay physical method completion beyond a timeout, as with standard synchronization primitives; no hard real-time wall deadline is claimed.
Reentrancy intentionally bypasses queued contenders while the same owner retains the outer lock; long critical sections or nested work can still cause honest 10-second timeouts.
FIFO does not establish the root cause of the observed original concurrency failure; barging remains a hypothesis.
memory_and_cost: Permanent registry path retention is unchanged. Each gate adds a Condition/RLock and deque; each live waiter adds an explicit token in addition to Condition waiter state. Tokens are removed on completion/timeout/exception.

notify_all on release and token removal can create a thundering herd. deque.remove is linear in current queue size. Throughput/latency effects require existing focused tests and measured qualification.

_state_for retains eager setdefault construction, so a new discarded gate is allocated even for existing keys; this pre-existing pattern now constructs more objects. No registry/cache redesign is recommended in this proposal.
qualification: No proposal applied or test workload executed by reviewer; production source remains unchanged. Do not apply until zero-timeout reentrancy is resolved and public fairness/timeout/interruption/ownership regressions plus unchanged frozen event-concurrency test pass. No performance, convergence or release-ready claim.
